sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Kafka and event-driven architecture interview questions cover the messaging system that powers most modern Java backends — Kafka architecture (brokers, topics, partitions, consumer groups, ISR), delivery semantics (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once), idempotent consumers, the outbox pattern, schema evolution, Kafka Streams vs Flink vs Spark Streaming, the saga pattern with choreography, CQRS and event sourcing, and Spring Kafka / Spring Cloud Stream. For RabbitMQ-specific questions (exchange types, routing, DLX), see the dedicated RabbitMQ page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three big questions for any event system:

1. **Delivery semantics** — at-most / at-least / exactly-once.
2. **Ordering** — per-partition (Kafka) vs per-queue (RabbitMQ).
3. **Durability** — acks, replication factor, ISR, fsync vs not.

Kafka = log; RabbitMQ = router; SQS = simple queue. Pick by **fit-for-purpose**, not hype.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Exactly-once** is delivery + processing; both must be idempotent.
- **Outbox pattern** — write event in same DB tx as state change, relay to broker.
- **CQRS** — read/write split; events update a denormalised read model.
- **Kafka partition count** is forever — picking it too low costs a topic re-create.
- **Consumer rebalances** — the silent latency spike during deploys.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd publish events via the outbox so the DB write and broker write are atomic, partition the topic by <natural key> for ordering, run consumers as idempotent (`UPSERT` keyed by event id), and watch for consumer-lag + rebalance frequency in observability."*
